sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the board really asking, and which numbers frame the answer?
criteria: Derives the overrun ($6.6M, 36.7%) and its gross effect on margin (27.5 bp) against the 10 bp cushion
Shows $17.7M of $18M is already spent, so the year cannot return to plan
Splits the overrun by cause: success (service agent), slippage (forecasting), waste (marketing and copilot)
Nets the extra savings ($3.6M) against the overrun before judging guidance

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake in the update, and how do you bring each along before the meeting?
criteria: Includes the audit committee chair and a pre-brief before the meeting
Agrees the net figure and Q4 actions with the CFO before the deck is written
Names the CMO as the stakeholder who loses, and what they are offered
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What framings or asks could you bring to the board, and how does each fare?
criteria: Includes at least report-only, cut-to-plan and a re-base option on one table
Shows cut-to-plan only works by stopping the service agent during the holiday peak
Compares each option's net hit to operating profit against the 10 bp cushion

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, what do you give up, and when would you revisit?
criteria: Makes one recommendation with the Q4 actions taken before the meeting
Derives the year-end figure ($22.475M) from the marketing pause and seat cut
Says which actions are reversible and that board trust is the irreversible part
Gives revisit triggers that can be measured (a 10% quarterly overrun, a repeat-contact rise)

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What did each initiative cost and return, and what is the net effect on the plan?
criteria: Shows cost and measured value per initiative, including that marketing's range includes zero
Derives the net hit after actions: $0.875M, about 3.6 bp
Gives the all-in cost including the AI team ($28.8M) and labels the $210k assumption
Derives the agent's unit economics ($4.13 against $7.00 a contact)

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who owns spend and who owns value from now on?
criteria: Names a business owner accountable for each initiative's value number
Keeps one accountable owner for portfolio spend and gates
Sets an escalation rule for overruns before money is spent

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens between now and the board, and over the next year?
criteria: Takes the Q4 actions and the CFO sign-off before the board meeting
Schedules the audit chair pre-brief before the deck is final
Has a dated gate with a measurable condition for the forecasting tranche

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could go wrong next, and what controls it?
criteria: Names a second surprise as the main risk, not the spend already made
Has a quality guard on the service agent it is scaling
Builds the overrun trigger and tranche gate into the budget, not into a policy note

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How will the board know next year is working?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Measures the service agent per resolved contact, not as a fixed budget
Reports value signed by business owners and reconciled by finance, not usage counts

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What exactly do you say in the room?
criteria: Gives an opening line that states the overrun and the net margin effect in the first sentence
Shows one slide with all five initiatives, their spend, value and call
Answers 'why trust next year's number?' with priced and gated lines, not a promise
Answers 'why not stop?' with the cost of stopping the service agent
